questions.question: In pre-industrial rural England, why were cottagers and poor peasants eager to work for urban merchant clothiers?
options: Open fields were disappearing and commons were being enclosed, so small plots could not generate enough livelihood without supplementary wage work
They were legally forbidden from farming wheat
They wanted to migrate permanently to London to become actors
Peasant households had no children or family members to support
questions.explanation: With the enclosure of common pastures and loss of customary foraging rights, poor peasants could no longer survive on their tiny farm plots alone. Advances from merchants allowed whole families to earn cash wages without leaving their villages.

questions.question: Why did manufacturers in late nineteenth-century India use printed calendars as a major advertising medium?
options: The British government made calendars the only legal advertising tool
Unlike newspapers and magazines, calendars were useful to and seen by illiterate consumers in homes, tea shops, and offices all year round
Calendars were made of silk and could be recycled as clothing
Newspapers were banned throughout India
questions.explanation: Calendars were hung on walls in homes, shops, and offices and remained visible day after day to literate and illiterate people alike, ensuring constant brand recall.

If royal personages used or approved of the product, its quality was beyond question and consumers should trust it
Consumers would be arrested if they failed to purchase the product

Nearly 85%
Around 40%

questions.question: In textile production, what does the process of 'carding' involve?
options: Weaving threads together to make finished cloth
Dyeing yarn in bright chemical colours
Stamping prices and company trademarks on cloth bundles
The process in which raw cotton or wool fibres are prepared and untangled prior to spinning
questions.explanation: Carding is the essential preliminary process where tangled raw fibres (cotton or wool) are cleaned, straightened, and prepared for spinning into yarn.

He became the managing director of the British managing agency
He began demanding money, gifts, and kickbacks for securing jobs and started controlling the personal lives of workers
